First listed 2026-05-21 · article

A Conspiracy of Credit, Part III: How the Greatest Fraud in Human History Happened - and What It Means for Private Credit Today

Eisman explains securitization and mortgage-era due-diligence failures, then argues that software concentration, retail liquidity promises and insurer links create private-credit vulnerabilities. Documented underwriting misconduct supports his central historical concern, but several absolutes fail: MBS predates the 1980s, Denmark has a substantial 30-year fixed mortgage market, some due-diligence samples expanded, and consumer mortgages can be modified. Civil RMBS enforcement contradicts broad claims that nothing happened without settling particular criminal-referral outcomes. The 2027-2028 refinancing scenario remains unfinished; universal private-software valuation losses and undated credit-cycle predictions remain unproved.

Substack · 2026-05-21 ↗
Substantive article review with paragraph references. Distinguishes persuasive mechanisms from overgeneralized history, unverified market estimates, normative judgments and actual future deadlines. The specific criminal-accountability claim remains unresolved rather than rebutted with unrelated originator cases.

  • Financial Crisis Inquiry Report, pages 165-169 · 2011-01
    Clayton classified 28% of sampled loans as deficient during January 2006-June 2007; 39% of those were waived in. Sampling methods varied. The report documents underwriting representations inconsistent with known exceptions, while not declaring every exception fraudulent.
  • Goldman Sachs agrees to pay more than $5 billion over RMBS · 2016-04-11
    The $5.06 billion civil settlement and agreed facts document knowing underwriting misrepresentations and typically unexpanded due diligence. It preserved criminal liability and does not establish the disposition of a particular FCIC criminal referral.

Conditional reasoning

Enterprise value equals multiple times the relevant earnings measure. A 50% multiple decline leaves value unchanged if earnings double. Equity value equals enterprise value minus net debt, so a public equity-price change is not a universal private enterprise-value change.

Assessment test: Value each asset using current cash flows, debt and appropriate comparable multiples.

Conditional reasoning

How he reasons here

  • Trace cash flows and loss seniority through securitization.
  • Separate collateral risk from repackaged security notional.
  • Inspect sampling design before extrapolating defects.
  • Distinguish civil enforcement from specific criminal referrals.
  • Match liquidity promises to underlying loan liquidity.
  • Separate public equity prices from private enterprise values.
  • Track maturity cohorts and sponsor equity support.
  • Include affiliated insurers in exposure mapping.
